card.name: Drug-pair interaction statements, partner drug next
card.fires_on: Words right after a first drug is named in a drug-interaction sentence, where a second interacting drug is about to be named. Examples are "and" in "between X and", "co-administered" before "with", and the start of a drug name after "that".

modes.label: Joining word between two drugs
modes.description: The word "and" or a comma after the first drug, just before the second drug in an interaction statement.
modes.example: There was no significant pharmacokinetic interaction between fluconazole<< and>> azithromycin.

modes.label: Co-administered, before with
modes.description: The ending of "co-administered" or "coadministered" after a drug name, right before "with" and another drug.
modes.example: However, diazepam co-administer<<ed>> with olanzapine increased the orth

modes.label: Drug name as sentence subject
modes.description: The start or end of a drug name, or a verb like "does", that opens a clause about its effect on another drug.
modes.example: Diazepam<< does>> not alter the pharmacokinetics of pro

card.writes: It pushes against words like relationship, interaction and "with", so it seems to shape what comes after the drug pair is set up.
card.plain: It fires in drug-interaction sentences just after the first drug is named, when the second drug is about to follow.
